mainTopic: Bathroom safety and health advice, the size of a shard for carrying on שבת, and the opening of the פרק on עבודה זרה and טומאת משא.
overview: This amud opens at the end of a story about כשפים, listing careless habits, like wiping with a shard, that expose a person to harm. רב הונא then urges his son רבה to learn from רב חסדא, whose bathroom advice protects human life. The גמרא brings practical disputes about wiping: a stone versus a shard, settled by reading the ברייתא as smooth vessel rims, and a stone versus grasses, settled by distinguishing moist from dry. It continues with health advice about holding it in, what to do when one cannot go, and walking before a long meal. A new משנה then debates how big a pottery shard must be to make one liable for carrying it on שבת. The גמרא shows that רבי מאיר's fire-scooping size is larger than רבי יוסי's and explains how רבי מאיר reads the end of the פסוק. The פרק המוציא יין ends with a הדרן. A new פרק opens with רבי עקיבא's source that an idol makes impure through carrying, like a נדה, and the גמרא begins by quoting a related משנה whose discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Habits that protect from witchcraft
steps.stepSummary: The end of the earlier story. The sorceress explains she cannot harm the חכמים because they avoid three careless habits.
steps.simpleTranslation: For you do not wipe yourselves with a shard, you do not kill lice on your clothes, and you do not pull a vegetable out of a gardener's tied bundle and eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story in which a sorceress admits she has no power over the חכמים, because they avoid certain habits that give כשפים a hold on a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each habit listed here is treated as an opening for harm through כשפים. The first one, wiping with a shard (חרס), sets up the practical discussion about wiping that comes later here.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רב הונא will soon say a person should not wipe with חרס: it carries danger.

phrases.english: for you do not wipe yourselves with a shard,
and you do not kill lice on your garments,
and you do not pull out a vegetable
and eat it from the bundle that the gardener tied.
phrases.notes: That is, eating from the bundle before it is untied.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and closes the sorceress story earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wiping with a shard, killing lice on one's clothes, and eating from a tied bundle expose a person to כשפים.

steps.title: רב הונא asks why רבה avoids רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא asks his son רבה why he does not attend the lectures of רב חסדא, whose teachings are sharp.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to his son רבה: Why aren't you found before רב חסדא, whose teachings are so sharp?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. רב הונא asks his son why he is not learning by רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא praises רב חסדא as a teacher with sharp, incisive teachings. His question sets up רבה's complaint in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: You are found / you are present

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא לְרַבָּה בְּרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna said to Rabba his son:
What is the reason you are not found
before Rav Chisda,
whose teachings are sharp?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story, connected to the earlier one by the shared theme of the bathroom.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבה does not go to learn by רב חסדא.

steps.title: רבה complains that רב חסדא teaches everyday matters
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that רב חסדא only teaches him everyday matters, such as how to behave in the bathroom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Why should I go to him? When I go, he occupies me with worldly matters. For example, he told me that someone who enters the bathroom should not sit down abruptly and should not strain too much, because the rectum rests on three 'teeth.' If those teeth slip out of place, he could come to danger.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains why he stays away: he feels רב חסדא teaches health and bathroom advice instead of Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה calls this advice מילי דעלמא, meaning ordinary worldly topics. His example is the warning not to sit abruptly or strain too hard, because the muscles (the 'teeth') holding the rectum could slip and cause real danger.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'teeth' here are not mouth teeth. They are the muscles that hold the rectum in place.

phrases.english: He said to him: Why should I go to him?
For when I go to him
he occupies me with worldly matters.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: מַאן דְּעָיֵיל לְבֵית הַכִּסֵּא
phrases.english: He told me: One who enters the bathroom
should not sit down abruptly,
and should not strain too much —
because the rectum rests on three 'teeth,'
and perhaps the teeth of the rectum will slip out
and he will come to danger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב חסדא teaches everyday matters, such as bathroom safety, rather than Torah.

steps.title: רב הונא: this protects life, so go all the more
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rejects his son's complaint. Teaching that protects human life is no small thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He is dealing with the lives of people, and you call it worldly matters?! All the more so, go to him!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא pushes back hard: the advice רבה dismissed is about saving lives, so he should go to רב חסדא even more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's reason for staying away is turned around into a reason to go. Guidance that protects health is part of Torah wisdom and not trivial. That is why רב הונא concludes with כל שכן.
steps.whatToRemember: A Torah teacher's guidance about health and safety is counted as dealing with human life, not 'mundane matters.'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הוּא עָסֵיק בְּחַיֵּי דִּבְרִיָּיתָא
phrases.english: He said to him: He is dealing with the lives of people
and you say 'worldly matters'?!
All the more so, go to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבה's reasoning from the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבה's judgment that רב חסדא's teaching is unimportant.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Advice that prevents danger to life is vital, not mundane.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבה should certainly attend רב חסדא's lectures.

steps.title: Dispute: stone or shard for wiping
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says to wipe with a stone rather than a shard. רב חסדא says the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he has a stone and a shard in front of him: רב הונא says he wipes with the stone and not with the shard. רב חסדא says he wipes with the shard and not with the stone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a practical dispute: which item a person should choose for wiping when both a stone and a shard are available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא avoids the shard because it can injure a person and is linked to the danger of כשפים mentioned in step 1. רב חסדא prefers the shard; one explanation is that this is because the stone is set aside (on שבת) in a way the shard is not.

phrases.english: If there were before him a stone and a shard,
Rav Huna said: He wipes with the stone
and does not wipe with the shard,
and Rav Chisda said: He wipes with the shard
and does not wipe with the stone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to practical הלכה about wiping, following up on the shard danger from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: stone, not shard. רב חסדא: shard, not stone.

steps.title: A ברייתא contradicts רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules exactly like רב חסדא, which seems to refute רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If there were before him a stone and a shard, he wipes with the shard and not with the stone. This is a refutation of רב הונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא whose wording matches רב חסדא, so רב הונא appears to be refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא carries the weight of a source from the תנאים, and an אמורא like רב הונא cannot simply disagree with it. The word תיובתא signals a very strong attack.

phrases.english: They challenged: If there were before him a stone and a shard —
he wipes with the shard and does not wipe with the stone,
a refutation of Rav Huna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's position from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that one should not wipe with a shard.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly prefers the shard, which directly contradicts רב הונא.

steps.title: רפרם בר פפא: the ברייתא means smooth vessel rims
steps.stepSummary: רפרם בר פפא defends רב הונא. The ברייתא speaks of the smooth rims of vessels, not sharp shards.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם בר פפא explained it before רב חסדא according to רב הונא: It refers to the rims of vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is reinterpreted so that it no longer contradicts רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'חרס' in the ברייתא is a smooth rim of a broken vessel, which poses no danger. רב הונא only forbade an ordinary sharp shard, so his position stands.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא, a smooth vessel rim is allowed; a sharp shard is avoided.

phrases.aramaic: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
phrases.english: Rafram bar Pappa explained it before Rav Chisda
according to Rav Huna:
It refers to the rims of vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא permits any shard, which contradicts רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers only to smooth rims of vessels, which are safe, so רב הונא is not refuted.

steps.title: Dispute: stone or grasses for wiping
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רב המנונא disagree about whether to prefer a stone or grasses.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he has a stone and grasses in front of him: רב חסדא and רב המנונא disagree. One says he wipes with the stone and not with the grasses. The other says he wipes with the grasses and not with the stone.
steps.whatsHappening: A new, parallel dispute: this time the choice is between a stone and grasses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not say which אמורא holds which view; it says only 'one said' and 'one said.' The question is whether grasses are fine to use or should be avoided.

phrases.english: If there were before him a stone and grasses,
Rav Chisda and Rav Hamnuna disagree:
One said: He wipes with the stone
and does not wipe with the grasses,
and one said: He wipes with the grasses
and does not wipe with the stone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case to step 5, using grasses instead of a shard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One view prefers the stone over grasses; the other prefers grasses over the stone.

steps.title: A ברייתא warns against wiping with flammable things
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says wiping with anything fire can burn causes harm, which challenges the view that permits grasses.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: One who wipes with something that fire can burn, his lower 'teeth' fall out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view that allows wiping with grasses, since grasses burn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that flammable materials harm the 'lower teeth,' the supporting muscles mentioned earlier in step 3. If so, how can anyone permit wiping with grasses?

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: הַמְקַנֵּחַ בְּדָבָר שֶׁהָאוּר שׁוֹלֶטֶת בּוֹ
phrases.english: They challenged: One who wipes with something that fire controls,
his lower teeth fall out!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הַמְקַנֵּחַ בְּדָבָר שֶׁהָאוּר שׁוֹלֶטֶת בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the view in step 8 that permits grasses.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that one may wipe with grasses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Grasses are flammable, and the ברייתא says flammable things cause bodily harm.

steps.title: Moist grasses versus dry grasses
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. Moist grasses are allowed; dry grasses are the dangerous flammable material.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: This refers to moist grasses, and that refers to dry grasses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by splitting the case: the ברייתא's warning applies only to dry grasses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moist grasses do not count as 'something fire controls,' so wiping with them is safe. Dry grasses are flammable and fall under the ברייתא's warning.
steps.whatToRemember: Moist grasses may be used for wiping; dry, flammable grasses should be avoided.

phrases.english: It is not difficult: This refers to moist ones,
that refers to dry ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּלַחִין, הָא בִּיבֵשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All grasses count as flammable and harmful.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only dry grasses are harmful; moist grasses are permitted.

steps.title: Dispute over the harm of holding it in
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רבינא disagree about what harms a person who needs to relieve himself but holds it in.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone needs to go to the bathroom and does not go, רב חסדא and רבינא disagree. One says an evil spirit takes hold of him. The other says a foul odor takes hold of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps giving health advice about the bathroom. It brings two opinions about what harm comes to someone who holds it in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that holding it in is harmful. They only disagree about what the harm is. One calls it a רוח רעה, a spiritual danger. The other calls it a רוח זוהמא, a physical foul odor or bad breath.

keyTerms.meaning: One who needs to relieve himself
A foul odor or spirit of filth
One said (we are not told which sage said which)

phrases.english: One who needs to relieve himself and does not do so,
Rav Chisda and Ravina disagree:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: רוּחַ רָעָה שׁוֹלֶטֶת בּוֹ,
phrases.english: One said: an evil spirit dominates him;

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: רוּחַ זוּהֲמָא שׁוֹלֶטֶת בּוֹ.
phrases.english: and one said: a foul odor dominates him.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אָמַר: רוּחַ רָעָה שׁוֹלֶטֶת בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of bathroom-related health advice, now about holding it in.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Holding it in is harmful. It is either a רוח רעה or a רוח זוהמא.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the foul-odor view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא compares eating while needing to go to heating a dirty oven, and calls this the start of a foul odor.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports the one who said a foul odor takes hold of him. It says: someone who needs to go and eats anyway is like an oven heated on top of its old ashes. That is the beginning of a foul odor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up the opinion of רוח זוהמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating while the body is full is like lighting a fire on top of old ashes. The ashes heat up and give off a stench. The ברייתא actually uses the words רוח זוהמא, so it matches that opinion directly.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא like the one who said
His orifices (a polite way of saying he needs the bathroom)

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with the one who said
a foul odor dominates him,
as it was taught: One who needs to relieve himself and eats

phrases.aramaic: דּוֹמֶה לְתַנּוּר שֶׁהִסִּיקוּהוּ עַל גַּב אֶפְרוֹ,
phrases.english: is like an oven that was heated on top of its ashes,
and this is the beginning of a foul odor.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר רוּחַ זוּהֲמָא שׁוֹלֶטֶת בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports one side of the dispute in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that רוח זוהמא dominates him
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא comparing it to an oven heated over its ashes, which uses the words רוח זוהמא

steps.title: Tips for someone who cannot go
steps.stepSummary: Four opinions on what a person should do if he needs to go but cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone needs to go but cannot: רב חסדא says he should stand and sit, stand and sit. רב חנן from נהרדעא says he should move to the side, to a different spot. רב המנונא says he should rub that area with a pebble. The רבנן say he should divert his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new but related case: someone who wants to go but cannot. It lists four pieces of practical advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each sage gives a different technique. The first is movement, the second is a change of place, the third is physical stimulation, and the fourth is mental. The meaning of the רבנן's advice is unclear, and that sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He should move off to the sides
He should rub with a pebble

phrases.english: One who needed to relieve himself and is unable to,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: יַעֲמוֹד וְיֵשֵׁב, יַעֲמוֹד וְיֵשֵׁב.
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: He should stand and sit, stand and sit.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חָנָן מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא אָמַר: יִסְתַּלֵּק לִצְדָדִין.
phrases.english: Rav Chanan from Neharde'a said: He should move to the sides.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הַמְנוּנָא אָמַר: יְמַשְׁמֵשׁ בִּצְרוֹר בְּאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם.
phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said: He should rub with a pebble in that place.
And the Rabbis say: He should divert his mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from someone who will not go to someone who cannot go.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four techniques: stand and sit, move aside, rub with a pebble, or divert the mind.

steps.title: Diverting the mind should make it worse
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges the רבנן's advice. If he takes his mind off it, he will certainly not go.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: Just the opposite! If he takes his mind off it, he surely will not go!
steps.whatsHappening: A sage challenges the last tip. He reads 'divert his mind' as 'stop thinking about it' and argues that this would not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge depends on what 'divert his mind' means. If it means forgetting about the bathroom, then the person will lose focus and fail completely. The question pushes רב אשי to explain the phrase.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן דְּכִי מַסַּח דַּעְתֵּיהּ לָא מִפְּנֵי!
phrases.english: All the more so, when he diverts his mind he will not relieve himself!

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן דְּכִי מַסַּח דַּעְתֵּיהּ לָא מִפְּנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the רבנן's advice from step 13.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking one's mind off the matter would stop a person from going, not help him go.

steps.title: Divert the mind from other things
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the advice means to clear the mind of everything else and focus only on this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי answered him: It means he should take his mind off other things.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge by explaining what the words really mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase does not mean 'stop thinking about the bathroom'. It means 'stop thinking about everything else'. Read this way, it is advice to concentrate fully, and the challenge falls away.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read יסיח דעתו here as 'forget about going'. It means the opposite: push out other thoughts so he can focus.

phrases.english: He said to him:
He should divert his mind from other matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יסיח דעתו means to stop thinking about relieving himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: יסיח דעתו means to clear away other thoughts and focus on relieving himself.

steps.title: An eyewitness report backs רב חסדא's tip
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה מדיפתי saw an Arab stand and sit repeatedly until it worked, which supports רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה from דיפתי said: I myself saw a certain Arab who stood and sat, stood and sat, until it poured out of him like from a pot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a personal eyewitness account that supports רב חסדא's advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is evidence from real life, not from a text. The Arab did exactly what רב חסדא advised, standing and sitting, and it worked very well. This shows the advice is effective.

keyTerms.meaning: It poured out like from a pot

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya from Difti said:
I myself saw a certain Arab
who stood and sat and stood and sat
until it poured out like from a pot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the list in step 13 and supports רב חסדא's tip.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's advice to stand and sit repeatedly

steps.title: Walk before a long meal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא advises walking a set distance and relieving oneself before sitting down to a long meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Someone going in to a long, set meal should walk four אמות ten times. Some say he should walk ten אמות four times. Then he should relieve himself, go in, and sit in his place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the bathroom topic with a ברייתא about getting ready for a long meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking helps the body get ready to go. Relieving himself first means he will not have to hold it in during a long meal, which steps 11-12 said is harmful. Both versions add up to forty אמות; they differ only in how the walking is divided.
steps.whatToRemember: The health-advice section ends here. Holding it in is harmful, there are practical tips for when one cannot go, and one should prepare before a long meal.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One who enters a set meal

phrases.aramaic: יְהַלֵּךְ עֶשֶׂר פְּעָמִים שֶׁל אַרְבַּע [אַרְבַּע] אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: should walk ten times four cubits each,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: אַרְבַּע פְּעָמִים שֶׁל עֶשֶׂר עֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: and some say: four times ten cubits each,
and relieve himself, and enter and sit in his place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, related piece of advice that ends the bathroom-health section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before a long meal, walk forty אמות, relieve yourself, and then sit down.

steps.title: How big a shard must be to make one liable
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה gives three opinions on the minimum size of a pottery shard for liability when carrying it out on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A pottery shard: one is liable if it is big enough to put between one wooden beam and the next. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי מאיר says: big enough to scoop up fire with it. רבי יוסי says: big enough to hold a רביעית of liquid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the minimum size for liability when someone carries a pottery shard from one domain to another on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An object counts for liability only if it is big enough to be useful. Each תנא points to a different use. For רבי יהודה it is a spacer between stacked beams. For רבי מאיר it is a scoop for coals. For רבי יוסי it is holding a רביעית of liquid.

keyTerms.meaning: To scoop up or stoke the fire
A quarter of a לוג (a liquid measure)

phrases.english: MISHNA: A pottery shard:
enough to place between one beam and its fellow,
the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי לַחְתּוֹת בּוֹ אֶת הָאוּר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: enough to scoop fire with it.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כְּדֵי לְקַבֵּל בּוֹ רְבִיעִית.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: enough to hold a revi'it in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ חֶרֶס כְּדֵי לִיתֵּן בֵּין פַּצִּים לַחֲבֵרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It returns to the main topic of שיעורים for carrying on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The size of a shard for liability is debated: a spacer between beams (רבי יהודה), a fire-scoop (רבי מאיר), or holding a רביעית (רבי יוסי).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the general rule of carrying on שבת: liability depends on the smallest amount that people would consider useful.

steps.title: רבי מאיר brings a hint from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר admits he has no full proof but cites a פסוק in ישעיהו that speaks of a shard used to scoop fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: Even though there is no proof for this, there is a hint to it: 'There will not be found among its pieces a shard to scoop fire from the hearth.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר supports his own opinion with a hint from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נביא describes a vessel smashed so badly that not even a fire-scooping shard remains. This suggests that a shard of that size is still thought of as useful. רבי מאיר calls it only a זכר, a hint, and not a full proof.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no proof for the matter

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר,
phrases.english: Although there is no proof for the matter,
there is a hint to the matter:
"There shall not be found among its pieces a shard
to scoop fire from the hearth."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר, זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי מאיר supports his opinion from step 18.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's size: enough to scoop fire

steps.title: רבי יוסי turns the פסוק around
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי points out that the same פסוק continues 'to scoop water from a pit', which supports his own size.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to him: Is that a proof? The פסוק goes on: 'or to scoop water from a pit.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי rejects רבי מאיר's hint by quoting the end of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק also mentions a shard used to scoop water. So it can just as easily support רבי יוסי's size, holding a רביעית of liquid. A פסוק that fits both sides cannot settle the dispute.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives three sizes for a shard. The פסוק cited by רבי מאיר is matched by its own ending, which fits רבי יוסי.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה?
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to him: Is there proof from there?
"And to scoop water from a pit."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מִשָּׁם רְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי מאיר's hint from step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The use of the פסוק as support for רבי מאיר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The end of the same פסוק mentions holding water, which fits רבי יוסי's size.

steps.title: Whose shard size is bigger?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which minimum shard size is larger, רבי מאיר's or רבי יוסי's.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The scholars asked: Is רבי מאיר's measure bigger, or is רבי יוסי's measure bigger?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking a simple factual question: which of the two shard sizes is the bigger one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says the shard must be big enough to scoop fire. רבי יוסי says it must be big enough to hold water. It is not obvious which job needs the larger piece, so the גמרא asks.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars

phrases.english: GEMARA
It was asked of them (the scholars):
Is Rabbi Meir's measure bigger,
or is Rabbi Yosei's measure bigger?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה cited in steps 18-20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the two shard sizes, fire-scooping or water-holding, is physically larger.

steps.title: Logic points one way, the verse points the other
steps.stepSummary: Logic suggests רבי יוסי's size is bigger, but the פסוק suggests רבי מאיר's is bigger.
steps.simpleTranslation: By logic, רבי יוסי's measure is bigger. But from the verse, רבי מאיר's measure is bigger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a two-sided answer: common sense says one thing, and the פסוק says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Common sense says holding water needs a bigger, deeper piece than holding a few coals, so רבי יוסי's size would be bigger. The order of the פסוק, however, hints the reverse. The next step explains how the פסוק shows this.

phrases.english: By logic, Rabbi Yosei's measure is bigger,
but from the verse, Rabbi Meir's measure is bigger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21, presenting logic and verse as pointing in opposite directions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Logic favors רבי יוסי's size as bigger; the פסוק favors רבי מאיר's size as bigger.

steps.title: How the verse shows רבי מאיר's size is bigger
steps.stepSummary: A curse goes from big to small, so the fire shard, mentioned first, must be the bigger one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if you think רבי יוסי's measure is bigger, would the prophet first curse him with not finding a small vessel and then curse him with not finding a big vessel?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the 'from the verse' half of its answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A curse builds up by saying 'you won't have even a big thing, and not even a small thing.' It would make no sense to curse with the small item first and then add the big one. Since the פסוק mentions fire first and water second, the fire shard must be the bigger one, which is רבי מאיר's size.

phrases.english: For if it enters your mind
that Rabbi Yosei's measure is bigger,
would he curse him with a small vessel,
and then curse him with a big vessel?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the 'from the verse' claim of step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר's (fire) measure is bigger than רבי יוסי's (water) measure.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The order of the curse in ישעיהו: fire first, water second, so the items must go from big to small.

steps.title: אביי: the fire shard is for a big blaze
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משנה means a shard big enough to scoop fire from a large blaze.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Our משנה also means scooping fire from a large blaze.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds support that רבי מאיר's size really is large, explaining what 'scooping fire' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might ask how a fire shard could be bigger than a water shard. אביי answers that the פסוק and our משנה mean taking fire out of a large blaze, which needs a big piece. This removes the conflict with common sense.

keyTerms.meaning: To scoop or rake up (fire or coals)

steps.whatToRemember: Conclusion of this section: רבי מאיר's fire-scooping size is the bigger one, because it means scooping from a large blaze.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
[Our mishna too]
means to scoop fire from a large blaze.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 23 by explaining why the fire shard is large, which also settles the logic problem from step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר's measure is bigger.
steps.raayaSupportSource: אביי's reading: 'scooping fire' means from a large blaze, which needs a big shard.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's argument seems strong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's reply from the משנה and says he argued well, which leaves רבי מאיר needing an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'רבי יוסי says: Is that a proof?' רבי יוסי argued well against רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבי יוסי's reply in the משנה and agrees it is strong. This sets up the question of how רבי מאיר answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי pointed out that the same פסוק goes on to mention scooping water, so water should be the measure. The גמרא admits this is a good point. This is a challenge against רבי מאיר: why does he ignore the end of the פסוק?

keyTerms.meaning: Is there a proof from there?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Is there a proof from there?
He argued well to him,
Rabbi Yosei to Rabbi Meir!

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the debate in the משנה (steps 19-20) and endorses רבי יוסי's point.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's proof from the first half of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same פסוק ends with scooping water, so it seems to support רבי יוסי's measure, not רבי מאיר's.

steps.title: רבי מאיר reads the verse as a build-up
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר reads the פסוק as 'not only will a valuable item be missing, but even a worthless one.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר says the verse is a 'no need to say' build-up: there is no need to say that something people value will not be found, but even something people do not value will not be found.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers how רבי מאיר handles the end of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the פסוק builds up its curse. First it says a fire shard, which people value, will be missing. Then it adds that even a water shard, which people do not value, will be missing. So the end of the פסוק adds force to the curse and is not the measure for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no need to say (a build-up style)
Will not be found for him

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: the fire shard is the measure. The water part of the פסוק only strengthens the curse ('not even something worthless').

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir says it in a 'no need to say' style:
There is no need to say that something valued by people
will not be found for him,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ מִידֵּי דְּלָא חֲשִׁיב לְאִינָשֵׁי
phrases.english: but even something not valued by people
will not be found for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25 on behalf of רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the structure of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The end of the פסוק (water) is the true measure, as רבי יוסי claimed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק builds from valuable to worthless, so the water clause intensifies the curse and does not set the measure.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק המוציא יין
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the eighth פרק, המוציא יין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק המוציא יין.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line marking the end of the פרק המוציא יין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks that this chapter is finished and expresses the hope to return to learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One who carries out wine', the name of the chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'One who carries out wine'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion in step 26.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק המוציא יין is complete.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: an idol makes impure through carrying, like a נדה
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה: רבי עקיבא derives from a פסוק that עבודה זרה makes a person impure through carrying, just like a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי עקיבא said: Where do we learn that an idol makes impure through carrying, like a נדה? As it says: 'You will cast them away like a נדה; you will tell it: Get out.' Just as a נדה makes impure through carrying, so too an idol makes impure through carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה where רבי עקיבא brings a source that an idol passes on טומאה even when it is only carried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאת משא means a person becomes impure by carrying something, even without touching it. The פסוק in ישעיהו compares throwing away idols to distancing from a נדה. רבי עקיבא learns from this comparison that idols have the same carrying-impurity as a נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: Idol worship; here, an idol itself
A woman in her state of menstrual impurity
An ill or menstruating woman (another word for נדה)

steps.confusionAlert: Carrying here does not mean touching. A person can carry an idol with a stick or in a bag and still become impure, just as with a נדה.

phrases.english: MISHNA
Rabbi Akiva said:
From where do we know regarding an idol
that it makes impure through carrying, like a menstruating woman?
As it is said: 'You will cast them away like a menstruating woman,
you will tell it: Get out' —
just as a menstruating woman makes impure through carrying,
so too an idol makes impure through carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: מִנַּיִין לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An idol passes on טומאה through carrying, like a נדה, learned from the comparison in ישעיהו.

steps.title: Quoting a related משנה about a house next to an idol temple
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by quoting a משנה from elsewhere. If a person's house stood right next to a house of עבודה זרה and fell, he may not rebuild it in the same place. He must move four אמות into his own property and build there.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: If someone's house was right next to a house of idol worship, and his house fell down, he is not allowed to rebuild it. So what should he do? He moves back four אמות into his own land and builds there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening its discussion by quoting a משנה from another מסכת. This is a setup line: the גמרא is laying out this source so it can ask questions about it on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rebuilding the shared wall in its old spot would also help the house of עבודה זרה, because that wall would serve it too. So the משנה forbids rebuilding in the same place. The solution is to pull back four אמות into his own land, so his new wall does not help the idol house at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Adjacent, right next to (here, sharing a wall)
How should he act? (the משנה asking itself what the practical solution is)
Pulls in, moves back (into his own property)
Four cubits, a set amount of space

steps.confusionAlert: The question כֵּיצַד יַעֲשֶׂה is not the גמרא challenging anything. It is part of the quoted משנה itself, which asks and answers its own practical question. The גמרא's own questions on this משנה begin on the next amud.

phrases.english: Gemara: We learned there (in a Mishnah elsewhere):
phrases.notes: The quoted משנה is from מסכת עבודה זרה.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁהָיָה בֵּיתוֹ סָמוּךְ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
phrases.english: One whose house was adjacent to an idolatrous temple
phrases.notes: The two buildings shared a wall.

phrases.english: and it fell, it is forbidden to rebuild it.
phrases.notes: Rebuilding the shared wall would also benefit the idol house.

phrases.english: How should he act?

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹנֵס לְתוֹךְ שֶׁלּוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת וּבוֹנֶה.
phrases.english: He moves back four cubits into his own property and builds.
phrases.notes: His new wall then does not serve the idol house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the new משנה about עבודה זרה making a person impure through carrying, the גמרא opens by quoting a related משנה about עבודה זרה to set up its discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A house that shared a wall with a house of עבודה זרה and fell may not be rebuilt in place. The owner must move four אמות into his own land and build there.
